correctness.rationale: The isometric root-plus-weighted-difference identification is an explicit bijection onto real R ⊕_1 ℓ∞. The finite row expression yields exact operator norm and finite-rank upper bounds. The disjoint-support lower witnesses are weakly null in ℓ∞ (bounded partial signed sums prove this), hence every compact operator annihilates them asymptotically. Both inequalities give the unrestricted compact-operator essential norm. Polynomial α=1 is the divergent-harmonic boundary; α>1 has uniformly summable tails. The alternating symbols satisfy the exact limit identities; 90 independent finite-rational profiles corroborate row algebra but are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the unrestricted big-space essential norm for arbitrary positive edge weights and its α=1 summability/compactness transition, not the known c0 tail-row lemma, the 2013 α=1 compactness criterion, or a general row-coordinate substitution. The closest 2026 published little-space result explicitly excludes nonseparable big spaces. In the summable regime, the new compact big-space example fails to preserve the little space, so it is not a specialization of that theorem. Generic matrix essential-norm technology remains a genuine terminology/priority risk.
residual_risks: A more abstract published ℓ∞ matrix/Calkin row-tail theorem may imply the exact formula under another name; absence from searches is not a novelty certificate.
Older weight-varying tree multiplier papers or unpublished sources not indexed in accessible searches could cover parts of the polynomial-weight conclusion.
The α=1 compactness criterion and the little-space formula are known; no independent priority claim is made for those ingredients.

value.rationale: The exact distance to every compact operator answers a natural unresolved counterpart of the earlier multiplier estimates for a nonseparable function space. The summable-versus-nonsummable reciprocal-weight transition gives complete compactness tests across all polynomial weights, with a sharp qualitative boundary: for α>1 symbol decay suffices and compact multipliers may not preserve the little space, whereas α≤1 explicit decaying symbols have essential norm 2. This is structural rather than a single arbitrary parameter computation.
